growth_stages.name: Germination & Seedling
growth_stages.description: Emergence. Sow several seeds per hill so the stand can be thinned later.

growth_stages.name: Tillering & Vegetative
growth_stages.description: Thin to 2-3 plants per stand by week 2-3. Millet is extremely sensitive to early weed competition, so thinning and the first weeding belong here.

growth_stages.name: Grain Fill & Maturity
growth_stages.description: Grain fill and ripening. Harvest at 75-90 days; milk-stage grains rot if cut too early and ripe heads shatter if left too late.

operations.name: Land Preparation
operations.description: Minimal tillage on light sandy soils. Clear and open planting hills at the first reliable rain.

operations.name: Planting
operations.description: Downy-mildew-resistant certified seed, in hills 75 cm x 50-100 cm apart, several seeds per hill for later thinning.

operations.name: Thinning & First Weeding
operations.description: Thin to 2-3 plants per stand and weed, by week 2-3 after planting.

operations.name: Nitrogen Application
operations.description: A modest amount of nitrogen. Millet yields where richer cereals fail but responds to light fertility on very poor soils.

operations.name: Harvest
operations.description: Cut the heads at 75-90 days after planting.

operations.name: Drying & Threshing
operations.description: Sun-dry the cut heads and thresh.

validation_rules.condition: Land preparation cannot be logged before land clearing. The 30-day interval is the cross-crop default.
validation_rules.source: General cross-crop default (same pattern as the other crop files), not independently sourced to a figure for this crop. Flagged for agronomist review.

validation_rules.condition: Planting more than 30 days after land preparation is flagged. Planting before land preparation is blocked by the global sequencing rule. The 30 days is the cross-crop default.
validation_rules.source: General cross-crop default (same pattern as the other crop files), not independently sourced to a figure for this crop. Flagged for agronomist review.

validation_rules.condition: Flag the first weeding or thinning if logged after 21 days after planting: millet is extremely sensitive to early weed competition.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, section 4 (Pearl Millet)

validation_rules.condition: Hard block if the first weeding or thinning is logged before 5 days after planting.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, section 4 (Pearl Millet)

validation_rules.condition: Hard block if harvest is logged before 65 days after planting: milk-stage grains rot. The ruleset gives no upper hard block, only the warning in pearl_millet_r8b.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, section 4 (Pearl Millet)

validation_rules.condition: Harvest is expected at 75-90 days. Flagged before 75 or after 100 days after planting (heads shatter).
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, section 4 (Pearl Millet)

validation_rules.condition: Harvest can only be logged once per planting cycle for an annual crop; a second harvest record requires a new planting record first.
Global rule: no operation may be logged with a date earlier than the previous operation's logged date for the same farm/cycle (no backdating that would reorder the sequence).

weather_preferences.notes: The most drought-resistant cereal in Nigeria, grown in the extreme North (Sahel and Sudan savanna) where sorghum and maize struggle, and it matures very fast: extra-early types in about 75 days for short-rains windows. Often grown with groundnut, cowpea, sorghum or maize. No rainfall or temperature figures are entered because the sources found give none. Sources: master ruleset section 4; ICRISAT, Lake Chad Research Institute and Nigeria's Federal Ministry of Agriculture handbook on pearl millet in north-eastern Nigeria (2020, front matter only seen).

diseases.name: Downy mildew
diseases.symptoms: The most serious pearl millet disease in Nigeria and Niger, with yield losses of up to 50% reported from western Africa. The ruleset names downy-mildew wipeout as a cause of near-total failure.
diseases.management: Use certified downy-mildew-resistant seed. In a Nigerian trial the variety PEO 5984 showed lower severity and higher yield than Super SOSAT, and severity was lower at Bauchi than at Maiduguri.
diseases.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, section 4 (Pearl Millet); ICRISAT Open Access Repository, incidence of pearl millet diseases in relation to time of sowing in Niger and Nigeria (oar.icrisat.org/4857); a Nigerian downy mildew variety trial.

diseases.name: Smut and ergot
diseases.symptoms: Smut and ergot are widespread in Nigeria and Niger alongside downy mildew. No incidence figures found.
diseases.management: Not stated in the sources found. Flagged for agronomist review.
diseases.source: ICRISAT Open Access Repository, pearl millet disease incidence in Niger and Nigeria (oar.icrisat.org/4857).

pests.name: Striga (witchweed)
pests.symptoms: A major constraint named by farmers in a Jigawa State survey of 143 farmers, with low soil fertility, downy mildew and labour cost.
pests.management: Farmers mainly hand-pull Striga or hoe-weed. No further Striga guidance found.
pests.source: Participatory rural appraisal of pearl millet farmers in Jigawa State (core.ac.uk).

pests.name: Early weed competition
pests.symptoms: Millet is extremely sensitive to early weed competition.
pests.management: Thin to 2-3 plants per stand and weed by week 2-3 after planting; the first weeding is blocked before 5 days and flagged after 21 days.
pests.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, section 4 (Pearl Millet)

factors: timing of thinning and first weeding
yield_model.notes: Pass tier of the master ruleset: lower per hectare than maize or sorghum, but it survives where they fail.

Severe drought or downy-mildew wipeout; verify plot area and the disease history.
Standard range, lower per hectare than maize or sorghum but it survives where they fail.
Improbable for West African rainfed millet; almost certainly a unit typo.

yield_validation.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, section 4 (Pearl Millet). The ruleset states Pass as 0.3-1.5 and the first warning above 2.5, leaving 1.5-2.5 undefined, so the Pass band is extended to 2.5, as other crop files do. The ruleset has no zero-yield hard block for millet beyond a general loss-event log; the loss-event rule used by every other crop is kept.

version_history.changed_by: AgTrail Knowledge Base - new crop from the master ruleset
version_history.summary: Initial file for Pearl Millet, one of three ruleset crops that had no file (with Sorghum, added earlier, and Vitamin A Cassava). Operations, timing limits and yield bands come from the ruleset. Disease and pest entries come from cited ICRISAT and survey sources at lower confidence; no rainfall, temperature or pH figures were found, so none are entered. Workflow 'required' flags are provisional.
version_history.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, section 4 (Pearl Millet)
